name: Cobra Pose
intro:
Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana) is a gentle backbend yoga posture that helps strengthen the spine and open the chest. In this pose, the upper body lifts off the ground while the lower body remains grounded, resembling a cobra raising its hood. It is commonly practiced in sequences like Sun Salutation and is suitable for beginners as well as experienced practitioners.

Bhujangasana helps improve spinal flexibility and posture by stretching the chest, shoulders, and abdomen. It counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting and slouching, making it especially beneficial for people with sedentary lifestyles. The pose also stimulates abdominal organs, supporting digestion and improving circulation.

Regular practice of Cobra Pose not only strengthens the back muscles but also helps reduce stress and fatigue. It promotes deep breathing by expanding the lungs and chest, which enhances oxygen flow and boosts energy levels. With consistent practice, it contributes to better posture, increased flexibility, and overall well-being.

steps.text: Lie flat on your stomach with your legs extended and feet together.
Place your palms under your shoulders with elbows close to your body.
Press your hands into the mat and slowly lift your chest.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and shoulders relaxed.
Lift your chest upward while keeping your lower body grounded.
Gaze forward or slightly upward without straining your neck.
Hold the pose while breathing deeply.

benefits: Strengthens the spine and back muscles
Stimulates abdominal organs and improves digestion
Supports overall body balance and flexibility
avoid: You have severe back injury or spinal issues
You feel pain while bending backward
You are pregnant (avoid or consult a doctor)
You have wrist or shoulder injuries
You experience dizziness or discomfort during the pose
